lesson.intro: A, an and the are articles. They come before a noun.
points: Use [[a]] before a word that begins with a consonant SOUND: a cat, a ball, a yellow kite.
Use [[an]] before a word that begins with a vowel SOUND (a, e, i, o, u): an apple, an egg, an ice cream, an orange, an umbrella.
Listen to the sound, not the letter: [[an]] hour (silent h), [[a]] uniform (sounds like "you").
Use [[the]] for something special or already mentioned: I saw a dog. [[The]] dog was barking.
Use [[the]] for things there is only one of: the sun, the moon, the sky.

examples.note: an + vowel sound, a + consonant sound

examples.text: I saw a cat. [[The]] cat was black.

lesson.tip: Say the word out loud. If it starts with a vowel sound, use "an".
